body:
`tests/unit/test_ingest_batch_dirty.py::test_successful_import_marks_batch_dirty_without_hot_loop_http_calls`
fails identically on `origin/main` and on a feature branch when run locally
(Python 3.12.7, macOS), while CI's Fast Tests job reports the same suite green
on main.

Observed 2026-08-08 while running the full unit suite before pushing the #1438
DIRS_JSON fix. A/B'd against a clean `origin/main` worktree to confirm it is
not branch-related: `1 failed, 2 passed` in both trees.

So either the test asserts something about ambient environment state that
happens to hold on the CI runner and not on the dev Mac, or CI is not actually
running it. Both are worth knowing: the first makes the local suite noisy
enough that a real failure gets waved through as "that one always fails", and
the second means the assertion protects nothing.

Not chased in the DIRS_JSON PR because it is unrelated to that diff and
pre-existing. Next step is to diff the CI invocation against the local one and
check whether the test depends on Python version, a network-adjacent default,
or an env var the runner sets.
title: test_ingest_batch_dirty hot-loop test fails locally but is green in CI
